text:
Maria: Heads-up — product is planning to GA a new model next Tues, `lynx-13b-qx`. Wanted to share a quick token/sec projection and ask infra for risk + mitigation ideas.

Eli: rough numbers from the model team: 2.8k tokens/sec per request on p50 long-tail prompts, avg tok/request 900, expected qps 40 at peak for the first week. That gives ~36k tokens/sec aggregate.

Sam: 36k toks/s steady — what's our current global serving capacity in tok/s on preferred runtime (A100-80GB equiv)?

Eli: we measure capacity by GPU hours + observed tok/s per GPU. On our optimized runtime: ~9k tok/s per GPU under typical batching for 13B quant. So ~4 GPUs sustained to hit 36k, but that's excluding headroom, autoscale latency, and regional hotspots.

Maria: We expect burstiness from PLG onboarding and a marketing demo on launch day. I'd budget x3 peak bursts for first 48 hours. So planning target = 108k tok/s.

Sam: triple burst -> 108k toks/s => ~12 GPUs (108k / 9k). Also need cache warmup and prefix KV cache pressure. If all traffic lands in us-west-2 we'll saturate a few racks.

ops-bot: deploy-check: current free A100 pool by region: us-west-2=8, eu-central-1=5, ap-northeast-1=3 (based on reserved vs committed).

Ryan: cost note: incremental reserved capacity (monthly) vs on-demand burst credits — 12 additional A100s for a week of burst ~ est $63k in on-demand. Reserved commit would be cheaper long-term but needs lead time.

Jen: product ask: can we do staged rollout (canary + regional rollout) to reduce blast radius? Prefer US-only for day-0 then EU day+1.

Eli: yes — recommend staged rollout plus fallback to smaller model `lynx-7b-qx` for heavy tails. Route policy: prefer cheapest healthy variant, fallback within 200ms latency window.

Sam: operational plan I propose:
1) Pre-warm 6 GPUs in us-west-2 6 hrs before launch (warm KV cache + model weights in memory).
2) Autoscale policy update: scale-up threshold 60% queue depth -> faster ramp.
3) Enable region weight cap: max 55% of global qps per region to avoid hotspots.
4) Configure graceful degrade to `lynx-7b-qx` at 95% GPU utilization per pool.

Eli: autoscale config snippet:```json
{"policy":"aggressive","scale_up_window_s":30,"cooldown_s":90,"max_replicas":20,"min_replicas":2}```

Sam: also watch for network egress bottleneck — a single instance can saturate 10-12 Gbps with that tok/s pattern. If many small requests hit concurrently we could see queue spikes despite GPU availability.

Maria: Can infra run a synthetic load test with 40 qps/region simulating 900 tok/request patterns? Need results by EOD Fri.

Sam: I'll schedule a canary run tonight against a staging pool. Ops runbook will include commands to increase pool:```bash
# pre-warm
redwood infra scale --region us-west-2 --pool lynx-13b --replicas 6
# force warm cache
redwood infra warm-cache --model lynx-13b --prefixes-file ./demo-prefixes.txt
```

Eli: quick math summary for docs: baseline sustained target = 36k toks/s (~4 GPUs), conservative launch target (x3 burst) = 108k toks/s (~12 GPUs), recommended pre-warm = 6 GPUs + autoscale to 20 cap, fallback model option, staged rollout to limit region blast.

Maria: Ryan — any objections on short-term on-demand burst for the first 48h? We'll re-evaluate cost vs conversion.

Ryan: okay for one-week on-demand cap with a hard budget limit and alerting. I'll create budget + burn alert in billing console.

Sam: I'll post a short checklist in #eng-infra tonight and tag SRE on-call. Also will add a dashboard tile for tok/s, GPU util, queue depth, and network egress per instance.

Jen: Thanks — product will scope canary users and delay demo if we see issues. Please drop the load test results in this thread. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: sched: canary-load-test started at 1789805420, job id c97f4b. Expected run 30m.

Maria: perfect — we'll reconvene after the test.
